To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated that the conserved motif is essential for correct assembly of Kgp and RgpA into non-covalently attached complexes on the surface of P. gingivalis.
the conserved motifs in RgpA and in Kgp catalytic domains are required for oligomerization into cell-surface attached, non-covalent gingipain complexes.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the formation of the Kgp gingipain complex and the effect of disruption of this complex on the virulence of P. gingivalis.
understanding how gingipain oligomers are formed and how they are regulated.
the molecular mechanisms of gingipains assembly into oligomers and their secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conserved motifs are involved in the oligomerization of the Kgp and RgpA domains.
the motif in each domain is essential for correct posttranslatory processing and assembly of Kgp into a non-covalent functional complex.
the conserved motif is essential for the correct posttranslatal processing of the Kgp catalyic domain and assembly of the non-covalent Kgp complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conserved motif is a critical element for correct posttranslatal processing, assembly, and surface localization of gingipains.
the conserved motif is required for the oligomerization of the gingipain domains into non-covalently associated cell-surface attached gingipain complexes.
the motif in each gingipain domain is required for correct processing of the multidomain gingipain complexes, and that this is likely to be a general requirement for all gingipain complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oligomerization motifs in Kgp and RgpA are critical for the correct assembly of these complexes.
the motif in each domain is essential for the correct assembly of the gingipain complexes.
the conserved motifs are required for the formation of non-covalent oligomer complexes of Rgp and Kgp.
